overview: Minimal UART transmitter for 50MHz clock, 9600 baud, 8N1 frame. Triggered by tx_en, signals completion via tx_done. All outputs registered.

modules.name: uart_tx
modules.purpose: Convert 8-bit parallel data to a serial UART frame (1 start, 8 data LSB-first, 1 stop) at 9600 baud using a 50MHz system clock.
modules.internal_behavior: FSM with states IDLE, START, DATA, STOP. 13-bit baud counter counts 0 to 5207, asserting bit_tick for 1 cycle per bit period. Baud counter resets to 0 when tx_en is asserted in IDLE. 4-bit bit counter tracks frame progress (0-9). 8-bit shift register loads tx_data when tx_en is high in IDLE (load priority over shift). Shifts LSB-first on bit_tick during DATA state. tx_out and tx_done are registered outputs to prevent combinational glitches. tx_out register is driven by state: IDLE=1, START=0, DATA=shift_reg[0], STOP=1. tx_done register pulses high for 1 cycle when FSM transitions from STOP to IDLE. tx_en is sampled only in IDLE; when high, FSM transitions to START, baud counter resets, and bit counter resets to 0.
modules.reset_behavior: Asynchronous active-low rst_n forces FSM to IDLE, clears baud and bit counters to 0, clears shift register, sets tx_out=1, and tx_done=0.
modules.default_behavior: Line remains high (idle) when not transmitting. tx_en is ignored during active transmission. tx_done remains low except for a single-cycle pulse at frame completion.

design_steps.description: Implement complete uart_tx module with registered outputs, explicit load/shift priority, and baud counter reset logic.

assumptions: tx_en is level-sensitive but sampled only in IDLE to prevent mid-frame retriggering
No parity or flow control is implemented per request
All outputs are registered to prevent glitches
